question: Which solid materials were tested in the Saffire experiments, and at what oxygen levels?
claim: The Saffire experiments burned SIBAL fabric (Saffire-I and Saffire-III) and silicone, cotton-fiberglass SIBAL, PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex (Saffire-II), all near normal air, between 21.5 and 22.1 % O2, with no O2 reported for Saffire-III.
summary_student: Saffire-I burned a cotton-fiberglass fabric called SIBAL in air with 21.5 to 21.7 % oxygen, and Saffire-III burned the same fabric but its table does not give the oxygen level. Saffire-II burned several smaller samples (silicone, SIBAL, PMMA plastic, and PMMA with Nomex) at 21.5 to 22.1 % oxygen. So every Saffire burn with a known oxygen level was close to ordinary air, not the oxygen-rich air planned for a lunar base.
summary_professional: Across the 13 Saffire test rows in PSI: PSI-98 (Saffire-I) has 2 SIBAL fabric tests at 21.5 to 21.7 % O2; PSI-100 (Saffire-III) has 2 SIBAL fabric tests with no O2 in the table. PSI-99 (Saffire-II) has silicone (n = 4, 21.5 to 22.1 % O2), cotton-fiberglass SIBAL (n = 1, 22.1 % O2), PMMA (n = 1, 22.0 to 22.1 % O2), PMMA and Nomex (n = 1, 22.1 % O2), plus 2 rows with an empty material cell at 21.9 to 22.1 % O2. Saffire-II O2 values are marked approximate and were derived from measured CO2 production (table Note 1); no Saffire table gives pressure.

params.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT investigation, source_table, source_row, o2_pct_min, o2_pct_max, field_sources, lower(replace(investigation, '-', '')) || '_' || trim(regexp_replace(lower(coalesce(fuel, 'material cell empty')), '[^a-z]+', '_', 'g'), '_') AS key FROM tests WHERE investigation IN ('PSI-98', 'PSI-99', 'PSI-100') AND phase = 'solid') SELECT key || '_o2_min' AS name, min(o2_pct_min) AS value, '% O2' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_min')) AS source_columns FROM t WHERE o2_pct_min IS NOT NULL GROUP BY key, investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT key || '_o2_max' AS name, max(o2_pct_max) AS value, '% O2' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_max')) AS source_columns FROM t WHERE o2_pct_max IS NOT NULL GROUP BY key, investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT key || '_n_tests' AS name, count(*) AS value, 'tests' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT coalesce(json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.fuel'), json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_min'))) AS source_columns FROM t GROUP BY key, investigation, source_table ORDER BY name

method.formula: The values returned by the SQL query in params, one row per value, each with the source rows it used.

assumptions: Material names are taken as written in the PSI tables; SIBAL fabric (Saffire-I and Saffire-III) and cotton-fiberglass SIBAL (Saffire-II) are listed separately because the tables name them differently.
Each table row is treated as one test, and the O2 range of a material spans the lowest and highest values of its rows, including range cells and approximate (~) cells.
limitations: The 2 Saffire-II rows with an empty material cell are not assigned to any material; the cell may be a merged cell in the source, but this finding does not guess which material they are.
Saffire-III does not report O2, so this finding says nothing about its oxygen level.
No Saffire table gives pressure, so the results cannot be compared with reduced-pressure habitat atmospheres.
All Saffire burns were in microgravity near normal air; the finding does not cover enriched oxygen, partial gravity, or other investigations such as BASS or BASS-II.
Only the PSI-98, PSI-99 and PSI-100 tables in the snapshot are covered; later Saffire flights or published results outside PSI are not included.
warnings: Saffire-II O2 values are approximate and derived from measured CO2 production, not measured directly (table Note 1).

chart.idea: Range bars of the O2 levels tested for each Saffire material, grouped by investigation, with the number of tests on each bar and Saffire-III marked as O2 not reported.

graph.idea: Saffire-I, Saffire-II and Saffire-III linked by shared Saffire hardware and the shared SIBAL fuel, each pointing to its PSI table.
